Title: Prototype Pollution via Default Extended Query Parser (allowPrototypes: true)
Analysis:
When Express runs with the default query parser setting ('extended'), it parses incoming request query strings using the `parseExtendedQueryString` function. This function delegates parsing to the `qs` library with the `allowPrototypes` option explicitly set to `true`.

Under the `allowPrototypes: true` configuration, the `qs` library permits the parsing and traversal of properties on the proto object of parsed dictionaries. This allows an attacker to inject properties that directly mutate the global `Object.prototype`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker sends the following HTTP request to the Express server:

GET /?__proto__[polluted]=true HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-server.com

During the query parsing stage, Express invokes `parseExtendedQueryString('__proto__[polluted]=true')`. Under the hood, `qs.parse` processes this into:
obj['__proto__']['polluted'] = 'true'

Since `obj.__proto__` points to the prototype of all plain JavaScript objects, this results in:
Object.prototype.polluted = 'true'

This pollutes the prototype chain globally. Subsequently, any object in the Node.js application will inherit the 'polluted' property, potentially enabling Remote Code Execution (RCE) or Denial of Service (DoS) in other dependencies.

Title: Prototype Pollution via Query Middleware Default Configuration (allowPrototypes: true)
Analysis:
The query middleware in `lib/middleware/query.js` configures the options passed to the `qs` library. If `allowPrototypes` is not explicitly defined in the options passed to the middleware, it defaults to `true`. This causes any incoming query parameter parser using the standard query middleware to be vulnerable to Prototype Pollution.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker sends the following HTTP request:

GET /?__proto__[polluted]=true HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-server.com

The middleware parses the query string:
req.query = queryparse(val, opts);

With `opts.allowPrototypes` defaulted to `true`, this mutates the global `Object.prototype`, adding the property `polluted = 'true'`. This prototype pollution can lead to application logic bypass, Denial of Service (DoS), or Remote Code Execution (RCE) in down-stream libraries.
